clue.text: A nearby resident almost caught old Conservative doing u-turn, the rotter!

indicators.note: a vehicle doing a u-turn heads back the way it came, so the whole string is read from the end
almost means the word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: a local is someone who lives close by
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone living nearby nearly caught an old Tory politician changing his policy, and denounces him as a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing u-turn' turns A + LOCA + C + O + C (ALOCACOC) right round. 'the rotter' looks like an insult to the politician but means a drink that rots teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugary fizzy drink is jokingly a tooth rotter, and this cola is the most famous of them.

clue.text: See 20 across
Silence understood to mean trouble

parts.note: sh is the word said to call for silence
took, as in 'took his meaning', means understood

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet is taken to signal that something is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: SHTOOK is British slang, from Yiddish, for trouble, as in 'in shtook'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in shtook is slang for being in a difficult or awkward predicament.

clue.text: Times when one died entering brawls

indicators.note: one piece goes into the middle of another, as someone enters a room

parts.note: frays are fights or scuffles
the Roman numeral I stands for one
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Periods when somebody was killed after joining in fights.
explanation.definitionFit: Fridays are particular days, so they are times in the sense of recurring occasions.

clue.text: A fresh river mouth

parts.note: pert and fresh both mean cheeky or saucy
the Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A new estuary where a river meets the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river mouth' reads as one phrase, but 'river' is part of the wordplay and 'mouth' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is an opening, and a mouth is an opening too, as of a cave or bottle.

clue.text: Girl turning up with blokes in street given grief

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Sarah is a girl's name

indicators.note: the men are placed within the abbreviation for street

parts.note: blokes are men

explanation.surface: A girl appears with some men in the road and is given a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' applies only to the girl's name; 'in' signals the street abbreviation wrapping the blokes, and 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief, in the informal sense of hassle or trouble given by others, is what harassment amounts to.

clue.text: Posh wife embraced by little Dickensian, as was Jeffrey Bernard

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class or posh usage

indicators.note: one piece is held within another, as in an embrace

parts.note: Little Nell is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop

explanation.surface: A well-bred wife is hugged by a small character from Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Bernard was a British journalist whose absences from his Spectator column were famously explained as 'Jeffrey Bernard is unwell', later a play title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spectator's stock apology said the columnist was ill, so the clue alludes to that famous sentence.

clue.text: See 24 down
Face for the radio might be so?

definitions.text: Face for the radio might be so?

parts.words: Face for the radio might be so?
parts.note: 'a face for the radio' is a media cliché for someone not good-looking enough for television, that is, unattractive or homely

explanation.definitionFit: Someone said to have a face for radio is unattractive, which is what the adjective means for looks.

clue.text: Oven meal, but no starter

indicators.note: a meal without its starter course, read as a word without its first letter

parts.note: a roast is a meal of roasted meat

explanation.surface: A cooked dinner from the oven, served without a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oven meal' reads as one phrase, but 'Oven' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, a kind of oven.

clue.text: On which the day's business is prepared, or otherwise

definitions.text: On which the day's business is

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A document on which the day's business is set out, or something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges PREPARED OR; the definition runs on into the anagram fodder, so the clue reads almost as a single description.
explanation.definitionFit: An order paper is the printed agenda listing a parliamentary day's business.

clue.text: Pair of kings securing oil producers Russian money

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly inside

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, so a pair is two of them
OPEC is the cartel of oil-producing countries

explanation.surface: Two monarchs lock in a deal with oil states for Russian cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A kopeck is a Russian coin worth one hundredth of a rouble.

clue.text: Test foreign students about Nepal regularly, before university

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the students go round the rest

parts.note: élèves is French for pupils or students

indicators.note: in a down clue, before means coming above
regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: Overseas students sit an exam on Nepal, often, before going to university.
explanation.walkthrough: The ELEVEN PLUS was a British exam taken at about age eleven to decide grammar-school entry. 'regularly' takes N, P, L from Nepal.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleven-plus is a school examination, so it is a test.

clue.text: See 24 down
Doctor attending more anaemic Sicilians here

parts.note: anaemic people look pale, so more anaemic means paler
MO is a Medical Officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor treats people who are even more anaemic than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like an anagram signal, but it is MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Palermo is the capital of Sicily, so many Sicilians live there.

clue.text: Complaint of middleaged blokes creating an awful stink among unruly gatherings

indicators.note: among means placed amid the other piece

parts.note: mobs are disorderly crowds
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A dreadful smell rises from disorderly crowds, causing complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN BOOBS is British slang for fatty breasts on a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess chest fat is an informal affliction associated with men in middle age.

clue.text: Acknowledgment given when time-piece runs backwards

indicators.note: backwards means the letters are read from end to start

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Proof you were given when a clock begins to run in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' turns T + PIECE + R (TPIECER) right round. 'time-piece' looks like one word for a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is a written acknowledgment that payment or goods have been received.

clue.text: See 20 across
Bird appears creamiest topless

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, in a down clue the first letter

parts.note: most rich, two words, means creamiest

explanation.surface: A bird looks the creamiest of all once it loses its top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creamiest' must be expanded to MOST RICH before the first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a large flightless African bird.

clue.text: Influence others to ensure immediate success of liposuction, might you say?

definitions.meaning: to ... mark and have a noticeable effect on other people

definitions.text: to ensure immediate success of liposuction, might you say?
definitions.meaning: said aloud, the phrase can be heard as making one's present self svelte, which is what a successful fat-removal operation does straight away

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a sound pun: 'presence felt' heard as 'present svelte'.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert a noticeable influence is the idiom's meaning: people become aware of you.

clue.text: Piano kept in dry below A sharp

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means the second piece sits under the first
kept in means held inside the other piece

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A piano stored in a dry room, below a note of A sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sharp' looks like the musical note, but A is a piece and 'sharp' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp, of a manner or a turn, means sudden or curt, which is what abrupt means.

clue.text: Flap wings of thrush going through bumpy ride

indicators.note: going through means passing into the middle of the other piece
a bumpy ride jolts things about, so the letters are jumbled
wings are the outer edges, so the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A thrush flaps its wings during a turbulent flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumpy' gives DIER, the shuffled ride; 'Flap' is a noun for agitation here, not the bird's wing movement the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap is a state of agitated indecision, the same as a dither.

clue.text: One's dotty, seeing neat '60s teenager head over heels in love

indicators.note: turned head over heels, a word is upside down, read upwards in a down clue

parts.note: a mod was a smartly dressed 1960s youth
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A smart sixties youth falls head over heels in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head over heels in love' looks like one phrase, but 'head over heels' turns MOD into DOM and 'in love' gives IN + O.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a tile marked with spots, so it is a thing that is dotty.

clue.text: Line got reversed on page among stuff for cipher

indicators.note: among means set amid the letters of the other piece

parts.note: to cram is to stuff
RY, railway, is a line

indicators.note: reversed means read backwards

explanation.surface: A line of text was turned round on the page, among material for a code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' gives TOG; in an across clue 'on page' places it after P, and the whole run sits inside the stuffing word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptogram is a text written in code, a cipher.

clue.text: Hot filling seat that's hot!

indicators.note: filling means occupying the middle of another piece

parts.note: a pew is a church seat
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A heated church bench prompts the exclamation that it's hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Phew is an exclamation voicing relief or reacting to heat, as in saying it is sweltering.

clue.text: Advice to self-pitying curtains?

definitions.meaning: telling someone sorry for themselves to regain their composure
curtains are drawn shut by bringing them to meet in the middle

explanation.walkthrough: An old joke: what do you say to self-pitying curtains?
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means regain self-control, and curtains are literally drawn closed to meet.

clue.text: In sound, the perfect thing is to test depth

indicators.note: in sound means the word is as heard, not as written

parts.note: a plum is the best of something, as in a plum job

explanation.surface: In good sound, the ideal approach is to measure how deep something is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' also suggests water depth, which fits the definition nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb is to measure water depth with a weighted line.

clue.text: Struggle against first of chains during escape

parts.note: con, as in pros and cons, means against

indicators.note: during means inside the span of the other piece

parts.note: to do a flit is to escape, often to avoid debts

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter

explanation.surface: A fight against chains during a breakout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of chains' gives C, which 'during' puts inside FLIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A conflict is a struggle or fight.
